Count each fixed point once, without multiplicity; no invertibility condition is imposed on \(D\varphi_H^1(x)-I\) at a fixed point.
</problem>

10	
11	## 1. Lower bound
12	
13	We use the following standard spectral-invariant properties for a closed monotone symplectic manifold. Here the Novikov variable \(q\) denotes recapping by a sphere of area \(4\pi\).
14	
15	* \(c(a,H)\) belongs to the capped action spectrum whenever \(a\ne0\).
16	* \(c(qa,H)=c(a,H)-4\pi\).
17	* If the fixed-point set is finite and \(B\) is an ordinary homology class of positive codimension, then
18	  \[
19	  c(a*B,H)<c(a,H)
20	  \]
21	  whenever \(a*B\ne0\).
22	
23	The last assertion is the strict spectral Lusternik–Schnirelmann inequality. Its strictness does not require nondegenerate fixed points. In the Floer cap-product construction, one represents \(B\) away from the finitely many periodic trajectories. A trajectory meeting the marked-point constraint must then have uniformly positive energy. Sphere bubbles have area at least \(4\pi\). Approximation and continuity give the assertion for degenerate Hamiltonians as well.
24	
25	Write
26	\[
27	e=[M],\qquad A=[S^2\times\{\mathrm{pt}\}].
28	\]
29	For the monotone product in the question, quantum homology satisfies
30	\[
31	A*A=qe.
32	\]
33	Consequently,
34	\[
35	c(e,H)>c(A,H)>c(qe,H)=c(e,H)-4\pi. \tag{1}
36	\]
37	
38	If there were exactly one fixed point, there would be exactly one geometric one-periodic orbit. Since \(M\) is simply connected, all its cappings differ by sphere classes, whose areas belong to \(4\pi\mathbb Z\). Thus the entire action spectrum would be one coset
39	\[
40	a+4\pi\mathbb Z.
41	\]
42	Two elements of this coset cannot satisfy the strict inequalities in (1). Zero fixed points are excluded by spectrality as well. Hence every finite fixed-point set has at least two elements.

46	## 2. An explicit three-fixed-point starting map
47	
48	Put
49	\[
50	k=10^{1000},\qquad C=k\sqrt{1+k^2},\qquad \alpha=2\arctan k,
51	\]
52	and define
53	\[
54	f(r)=2r\arctan(Cr)-\frac1C\log(1+C^2r^2).
55	\]
56	Although \(r=|x+y|\) is not smooth on the antidiagonal, \(f(r)\) is smooth there: its Taylor series is a power series in \(r^2\).
57	
58	Let \(B_k\) be the time-one map of \(f(|x+y|)\). Setting \(m=x+y\), \(r=|m|\), it rotates both \(x,y\) about \(m\) through the angle
59	\[
60	\theta(r)=2\arctan(Cr).
61	\]
62	In particular, it is explicitly
63	\[
64	B_k(x,y)=\bigl(R_m x,R_m y\bigr),
65	\]
66	where
67	\[
68	R_m z=
69	\frac{(1-C^2r^2)z+2C(m\times z)+2C^2m(m\cdot z)}
70	     {1+C^2r^2}. \tag{2}
71	\]
72	
73	Let
74	\[
75	P_k(x,y)=\bigl(R_{e_1}^{\alpha}x,R_{e_2}^{\alpha}y\bigr),
76	\qquad
77	\psi_k=P_k\circ B_k.
78	\]
79	The map \(P_k\) is generated by \(\alpha(x_1+y_2)\), with precisely the Hamiltonian convention in the question.
80	
81	### Exact fixed-point calculation
82	
83	The fixed-point equations imply
84	\[
85	x=(p,t,kt),\qquad y=(t,q,-kt),\qquad
86	p^2+(1+k^2)t^2=q^2+(1+k^2)t^2=1.
87	\]
88	Thus \(q=\pm p\). With \(u=t\sqrt{1+k^2}\), the remaining equations factor as follows:
89	\[
90	\begin{array}{ll}
91	q=-p:&(u+1)(k^2u-k^2-1)=0,\\[2mm]
92	q=p:&(u+1)((k^2+2)u-k^2-1)=0.
93	\end{array}
94	\]
95	The second root in the first line exceeds \(1\). Therefore \(\psi_k\) has exactly these three fixed points:
96	\[
97	\begin{aligned}
98	s_k:\quad&
99	p=q=0,\quad t=-\frac1{\sqrt{1+k^2}},\\
100	n_k^\pm:\quad&
101	q=p=\pm\frac{\sqrt{2k^2+3}}{k^2+2},
102	\quad t=\frac{\sqrt{1+k^2}}{k^2+2}. \tag{3}
103	\end{aligned}
104	\]
105	
106	We will leave \(s_k\) untouched and replace the two points \(n_k^\pm\) by one degenerate fixed point.
107

110	## 3. Exact Darboux coordinates near the other two points

122	\]

127	Q=X+Y,\qquad

129	\]

136	\[
137	\begin{aligned}
138	Q_1'&=2P_2+\frac{4Q_2}{|Q|^2}+2,\\

161	## 4. A compactly supported planar merger

163	Here are explicit smooth cutoffs used below.

165	Let
166	\[
167	\ell(s)=\max(0,\min(1,2s-\tfrac12)),
168	\]

171	\rho_0(v)=
172	\begin{cases}
173	c_0\exp\!\left(-\dfrac1{1-16v^2}\right),&|v|<\frac14,\\

175	\end{cases}

178	\[
179	\Theta(s)=\int_{\mathbb R}\rho_0(v)\ell(s-v)\,dv.
180	\]

182	\[
183	\Theta=0\quad(s\le0),\qquad
184	\Theta=1\quad(s\ge1),\qquad 0\le\Theta'\le2.

191	\Theta\!\left(\frac{\log(100/r)}{\log2}\right),

235	## 5. The exact finite-\(k\) correction

237	This part also specifies the small correcting function uniquely, without any genericity choices.

239	Write
240	\[
241	\Phi_k(Q,P)=\bigl(\mathcal Q_k(Q,P),\mathcal P_k(Q,P)\bigr).

244	\[

251	\mathcal Q_k(Q,p_k(Q))=Q. \tag{11}
252	\]

254	\[
255	p^{(j+1)}
256	=p_0(Q)-\frac12 J\!

259	\]

342	## 6. A globally defined Hamiltonian kick
